did: PRODUCT -- found and repaired a field-level lie in the cashflow panel, then measured the repair on 1.04M real rows. DIAGNOSIS: the cashflow report's own NOTICE_DATE is not the filing date for any era we hold -- per-period median usable share inside the disclosure window is 0.7% pre-2010 AND 0.7% in 2010+ (anchors: 2010-03-31 median lag 391d, 2020-03-31 393d, 2025-03-31 393d, i.e. the stamp is roughly the NEXT YEAR's same-quarter filing), while balance is 98.96%/96.34% usable and income inverts the pattern (2.6% pre-2010 -> 89.4% 2010+). That is why r1102/r1103 had to disclose cashflow's first-announce face as ~90% deadline fallback. INSIGHT: all three statements are published in ONE filing event, so the date can be cross-certified inside the same (code, period). NEW scripts/fund_avail_filing_event.py (selftest 9/9): filing_event = min over the three faces' cached first_notice dates restricted to (period_end, statutory_deadline+90d], falling back to the deadline when no candidate is in-window (never early, never fabricated); caches joined INSIDE their period (r1102 law) with write-site assertions on row count, (code, period_end) uniqueness and avail_event >= period_end. RESULT (fallback share, published avail_first -> event face): cashflow 2010+ 91.7% -> 8.0%, pre-2010 84.9% -> 32.3%; income pre-2010 97.5% -> 42.4%, 2010+ 13.1% -> 12.5%; balance 2010+ 30.5% -> 5.2%, pre-2010 34.5% -> 29.6%. Per-period distinct first-announce dates: cashflow 12 -> 64.5 median, income -> 72, balance -> 64.5. Full window: 70.6% of cashflow rows (292,537) become available EARLIER than the published face, 21.6% of balance, 4.3% of income; identical 26.8%/77.1%/95.3%. CROSS-FACE CHECK: where two faces both hold an in-window stamp they agree EXACTLY (median |diff| = 0d across 50/17/14 periods), so the repair introduces no conflicting dates -- it only picks whichever sibling is valid for that period. Honest bound: 7.8-15% of rows (up to 42% pre-2010) still have no in-window candidate and keep the deadline fallback, and this face answers 'most credible never-early upper bound', not 'the true announcement date'.
